name: Page-header-lockup
purpose: The page-header region: an eyebrow or a breadcrumb, the page title, an optional meta line, a right-aligned action pair on the title row, and an optional tab strip on its bottom edge (the FOOT), arranged so the title stays legible and the actions collapse to their own row on a narrow container. ONE lock-up with three optional parts (s313-D28), not a set of arrangements. Composed ENTIRELY from existing gated/proposed atoms (Breadcrumbs, Eyebrow, Tabs, Button, Badge) — no new visual vocabulary, only arrangement. Itinerary row 115 (Layer 2, class NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled).

props.name: actions
props.$note: 0-2 Button instances (any tier), ALWAYS ON THE TITLE ROW (s313-D28). The organism does not draw a new button style.

props.name: showBreadcrumb
props.$note: The crumb-or-eyebrow switch: on a drill-down the breadcrumb REPLACES the eyebrow — never both (s313-D28).

props.name: showMeta
props.$note: The meta line under the title (a timestamp, a scope such as 'Consolidated position · GBP equivalent'). Replaces showBadge (s313-D28): the badge-count arrangement goes — a count belongs in a tab label or the content, not beside the title.

props.name: showTabs
props.$note: THE FOOT: on a page with sub-views the Tabs strip sits on the lock-up's bottom edge, where the page's views begin (s313-D28). Tabs keeps its own overflow script — a tab foot on a real page needs that script beside it (#312 F2: at 390 the demo's foot ran off the right edge without it).

$s313D28: THE LOCK-UP'S SHAPE, RULED FOR NOW. s313-D28 (#313, Dave by click on the pictures page, call 9, verbatim: 'Option 2, a foot for the tab strip' — the recommendation) with his comment, verbatim: 'Lets have this for now, but this is one component that I want to work on in the future its quite fussy at the moment' (W-313d3 — his future work, not redesigned here). The arrangement choice (simple / breadcrumb-tabs / meta-badge, #210) is REPLACED by the three switches the lock-up already carried — crumb or eyebrow (showBreadcrumb), meta line (showMeta), tab foot (showTabs) — with the actions always on the title row. The badge-count arrangement goes. Heights the #312 F2 run measured at 1440: as built 126px, with the foot 198px. Closes W-305e3.

variants.name: simple
variants.use: Eyebrow + title + a right-aligned action pair, every switch off. The default — most page headers need nothing more.

variants.name: with-foot
variants.use: All three parts on (s313-D28): breadcrumb in place of the eyebrow on a drill-down, title + meta line + actions on one row, and the Tabs strip on the bottom edge for the page's sub-views. The shape the pictures page drew as option 2.

tokens.title: borrowed from canon/type.css .t-cm-heading composite (32px/400) — never a raw declaration
tokens.breadcrumb: text/default + the '/' or chevron separator via Breadcrumbs.reference.html, unmodified
tokens.tabs: the full tabs/* token set via Tabs.reference.html, unmodified, including its own responsive overflow
tokens.$note: Every token above resolves through the ATOM's own manifest; this organism binds nothing new. The lock-up's own CSS (`.ph-*`) is flex arrangement only — no colour, no type-size, no radius declaration of its own.

responsive.$status: PROPOSED at #210 wave-5 (not ruled) — reflow verified in a real browser at 3 widths.
responsive.rule: Wide: title left, actions right, one row. Container <=560px (container-query, WCAG 1.4.10 reachable to 320px): the action pair falls to its own full-width row beneath the title, right-aligned. Tabs (arrangement B) collapses independently via ITS OWN unmodified ResizeObserver logic — this organism never re-implements tab overflow.
responsive.$note: s210-D3 discipline: the lock-up declares no width of its own; the container gives it one.

commonPatterns: inbox-style header with an unread count

accessibility.structure: The title is a single <h1> per page instance (heading order, 1.3.1); Breadcrumbs keeps its own nav landmark + aria-current; Tabs keeps its own role="tablist"/tab/tabpanel triad, all unmodified from the source atom.
accessibility.focus: Every borrowed atom keeps its OWN :focus-visible ring — the organism adds no new focusable element and no new focus style.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the title, breadcrumb, tab or button CSS instead of composing the existing atom — the #202 defect this brief names explicitly
Giving the lock-up a fixed width — s210-D3 reserves that for the container
Putting more than one <h1> on the page by nesting a second lock-up
Re-implementing Tabs' overflow collapse at the organism layer instead of leaving Tabs' own JS untouched
